rationale: Matthew 8:11 pictures many who "share the banquet with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven" (BSB), and Isaiah 25:6 pictures the LORD preparing "a banquet for all the peoples" on His mountain (BSB); the Pulpit Commentary states that Matthew's image is "taken from Isaiah 25:6." The grade stays at plausible because Matthew names no prophet and shares no phrase with Isaiah 25 beyond the banquet image itself, which the Wikipedia article on Matthew 8:11 (reporting France) calls a frequent idea in Jewish literature of the period. The verse's "from the east and the west" wording points to other texts instead -- Isaiah 43:5 ("I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west") and Psalm 107:3 ("from east and west, from north and south"), the first addressed to "Jacob" and "Israel" (Isaiah 43:1) and the second to "the redeemed of the LORD" (Psalm 107:2), both about gathering a scattered people rather than about foreigners -- which is part of why Davies and Allison, as Wikipedia reports them, leave open whether Matthew's "many" are Gentiles or diaspora Jews.
